transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (PM), Priya Desai (Product Ops), Marcus Lee (SRE), Elena Gomez (Eng Lead), Jordan Harris (Head of Product), Sofia Martinez (Eng Manager), Liam Patel (QA Lead)

[00:00:05] Alex Chen: okay uh let's get started thanks everyone for jumping on, I know this is the big Q4 launch readiness sync, try to keep to the checklist items, we'll go through risks then canary plan then actions.
[00:00:22] Sofia Martinez: hey Alex, quick note, we've got a QA window conflict on the 29th with a release in infra, so if we move the canary too late it collides, so keep that in mind.
[00:00:35] Alex Chen: good call, we'll surface that when scheduling, Elena can you give status on canary readiness?
[00:00:40] Elena Gomez: yes uh short version: canary plan drafted, smoke tests exist but we need to add KV cache warm-up and some longer tail latency checks, also need SRE sign-off on autoscaling knobs.
[00:00:55] Marcus Lee: autoscaling knobs - I'm still worried about sustained bursts. The reserved pool config for Dedicated will handle steady throughput but if the canary generates odd seq lengths we could see kernel selection thrash, meaning high p99.
[00:01:12] Jordan Harris: when you say kernel selection thrash, are you referring to the runtime choosing different kernels per sequence length? how often does that flip in practice?
[00:01:21] Marcus Lee: yeah so if the model's sequence length distribution varies a lot across requests the runtime might pick suboptimal kernels repeatedly, especially for quantized variants. It shows up in our perf runs. Not huge for small traffic but for canary at scale could matter.
[00:01:36] Elena Gomez: that's why the KV cache warm-up's important, and we should simulate the exact prompt patterns the product will send. Priya and Jordan, do we have representative prompt sets?
[00:01:48] Priya Desai: we do have a couple of them, I uploaded a starter set to the launch docs, link: https://redwood.internal/docs/q4-launch-checklist prompt-set-v2.csv, but I think we need to expand it with longer conversations.
[00:02:05] Liam Patel: QA flagged that some of the conversational flows include file attachments and tool calls, which exercise function-calling paths and increase tokenization overhead. Those flows need to be included in perf tests.
[00:02:19] Alex Chen: good — include those in the test matrix. Sofia, can you call out QA gaps?
[00:02:26] Sofia Martinez: sure, gaps are: lack of end-to-end for tool calls, not enough long tail latency checks, missing behavior tests for degraded models fallback. Also need deterministic checks that our rollbacks trigger correctly.
[00:02:41] Alex Chen: rollback behavior — Marcus, is that covered by current rollout infra?
[00:02:45] Marcus Lee: partially. We have automated fallback to smaller model variants and region fallback, but we don't have a fully automated canary failover that handles partial KV cache population. If the canary writes sticky caches, traffic switch can see cold cache misses.
[00:02:59] Elena Gomez: so we need a canary that both warms caches and validates cache consistency across instances. The playbook should include cache drain steps pre-swap.
[00:03:12] Jordan Harris: can we add a checkpoint: "cache warm and validated" before we promote? that seems reasonable.
[00:03:18] Alex Chen: yes add that to the checklist.
[00:03:23] [00:03:30] Alex Chen: switching gears to incident review — Marcus you led the postmortem last week, can you summarize key fixes?
[00:03:35] Marcus Lee: yeah, summary: root cause was an overloaded scheduling queue and a KV cache eviction cascade during a burst; fixes include rate-limiting at ingress, improved backpressure between batching and request queues, and a patch to the cache eviction algorithm to avoid cascading evictions. Implementations in staging; tests run but want more long-duration tests. We also found some misconfigured KMS rotation flags that complicated key access in the incident but that was secondary.
[00:04:02] Priya Desai: KMS rotation flags — security asked for a follow-up, are we scheduling that?
[00:04:08] Marcus Lee: Security is owning the rotation doc but I'll help verify in staging.
[00:04:12] Sofia Martinez: QA saw flakiness in the teardown of the cache nodes, sometimes tests left stray sockets, which caused the next run to fail. We'll add explicit teardown in harness.
[00:04:25] Liam Patel: noted.
[00:04:28] [00:04:40] Elena Gomez: on performance, SE team shared a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 from last week's bench. We hit p99 spikes when batching was disabled for some flows. The suggestion was to enable adaptive batching but cap max latency to 800ms for interactive sessions.
[00:04:58] Alex Chen: where's that spreadsheet? link?
[00:05:01] Elena Gomez: link in the deck: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/q4-perf-v1.xlsx, I flagged the rows with KV cache cold misses.
[00:05:10] Marcus Lee: adaptive batching is good but we need hard limits so we don't exceed SLO. Also the product needs to accept slightly higher p50 to reduce cost. Tradeoff decision needs product sign-off.
[00:05:22] Jordan Harris: Product is ok with a small p50 uplift if p99 is stable; what's the projected cost delta?
[00:05:29] Elena Gomez: estimated 6-9% decrease in cost per token if we let batching run at 30-50ms window, but p50 might move up 10-15ms. I'll add numbers to the doc.
[00:05:40] Priya Desai: can we get a one-pager tradeoff by end of the week?
[00:05:43] Elena Gomez: yeah, I'll put it together.
[00:05:46] [00:06:05] Alex Chen: security gating — we need SOC 2 checklist items completed before launch date, specifically the evidence for key management, audit logging retention, and SSO baseline. Marcus, can you confirm audit logs retention parity across Dedicated and Private deployments?
[00:06:18] Marcus Lee: Dedicated has retention enabled, Private deployments depend on customer config but for our launch we'll only certify Hosted + Dedicated. SSO baseline — we need SAML testing for the console flows, security is handling that.
[00:06:30] Jordan Harris: do we have any outstanding compliance ask from Sales/Legal for customers that could block launch?
[00:06:36] Priya Desai: Sales asked for a SOC2 attestation date, legal requested additional encryption-at-rest notes for on-prem. We've got draft answers in the security pack. link: https://redwood.internal/security/soc2-pack.pdf
[00:06:49] [00:07:00] Alex Chen: okay, timeline check: are we still targeting canary in staging on 2026-10-05 and full rollout during week of 2026-10-12? any objections?
[00:07:08] Sofia Martinez: that timeline is tight given QA windows, but workable if we get the checklist done this week and engineering prioritizes the warm-up scripts.
[00:07:18] Elena Gomez: engineering can prioritize but we need to freeze noncritical changes starting 2026-10-03 to stabilize.
[00:07:24] Marcus Lee: also note: we should schedule a dry-run rollback on 2026-10-06 to validate automated fallback; that's separate from the primary canary.
[00:07:33] Alex Chen: add dry-run rollback to plan.
[00:07:36] [00:07:50] Jordan Harris: going back to incident fixes, Marcus you mentioned backpressure between batching and request queues — does that require runtime changes or config tweaks?
[00:07:58] Marcus Lee: a mix. We shipped a config change that buys some protection, but a runtime-level fix will be a small code path to propagate queue-length signals; that might need a minor release.
[00:08:11] Elena Gomez: can we ship the config first for the canary and the runtime patch in the follow-up?
[00:08:15] Marcus Lee: yes, that's the plan. Config now, runtime patch in next minor.
[00:08:20] [00:08:30] Priya Desai: I want to be clear on communication: if canary hits trouble and we pause, who's the comms owner to update sales/support?
[00:08:36] Alex Chen: Priya you own comms, Jordan you'll backfill leadership updates. Also include a bullet for support KB to be ready with rollback steps.
[00:08:45] Priya Desai: noted.
[00:08:48] [00:09:05] Liam Patel: small QA ask — can we get a staging snapshot with realistic DB size for the canary? the tokenization and index sizes significantly affect perf.
[00:09:14] Marcus Lee: yes we'll provide a snapshot, but we need to ensure PII scrubbed; security to confirm allowed artifacts.
[00:09:21] Jordan Harris: security sign-off on scrubbed snapshot? who's that?
[00:09:25] Priya Desai: Security (Ana Kim) is on copy of the launch docs, she'll sign off.
[00:09:33] [00:09:50] Elena Gomez: one more perf risk: third-party logging added to the runtime increased serialize latency in last run. We should ensure logs are async and not blocking. Marcus can you validate?
[00:10:00] Marcus Lee: yep, we'll flip to asynchronous logging for canary.
[00:10:05] [00:10:20] Alex Chen: ok let's recap decisions and owners — checklist finalization (Alex/Priya), canary plan and smoke tests (Elena/Sofia/Liam), KV cache warm-up and benchmarks (Marcus/Elena), security gating (Marcus/Ana), communication (Priya). Dry-run rollback scheduled 2026-10-06. Canary in staging 2026-10-05. Full rollout week of 2026-10-12 pending canary.
[00:10:45] Jordan Harris: anything else on incident items?
[00:10:48] Marcus Lee: postmortem draft will go out end of day tomorrow, link in docs.
[00:10:55] Alex Chen: great. Any blockers we didn't surface?
[00:11:00] Sofia Martinez: none from QA side other than the 29th window conflict which we noted.
[00:11:05] Priya Desai: legal/security answers are in progress but we might need an extra day if reviewers ask clarifying Qs.
[00:11:12] [00:11:25] Alex Chen: ok thanks everyone. We'll share updated checklist and a short one-pager on the batching tradeoff. Meeting adjourned.
